name: gearbox
description: Per-prompt model and effort for Claude Code. By default an orchestrator keeps the main conversation on Opus to plan, brief and review, runs the work in one long-lived agent per model and splits independent parts across up to 6 agents at once; browser checks, long commands and git chores go to cheap subagents; and a live readout shows every agent's model.

code_model.title: Coding model
code_model.description: The model all code runs on. sonnet (the default), opus or fable fix it: every code turn, code-writing subagent and go-ahead to write code runs on exactly that model at your coding effort, in a subagent when the conversation runs another model, save a mechanical edit at one spot, which stays in the conversation (Fable always in a subagent, without asking first); other work keeps the rules. auto lets the rules pick it, as for any work: the session's model, handed up to a stronger one when the work calls for it. Also settable with /gearbox model.

code_effort.title: Coding effort
code_effort.description: Effort for writing code: every code turn runs at least at it, small edits included; answers and explanations follow their difficulty. Default xhigh; Anthropic suggests medium for Opus 5.5 if you prefer faster, cheaper turns. auto leaves delegation to the main conversation once it has read the work: deep, lane and fan-out hand-offs become advice whose default is to hand off (browser checks, long commands and git chores still go to agents), each agent runs on the model and effort its call names (effort medium to xhigh, a review on Opus at least, Fable asked first; with none named, gearbox picks), and the main conversation may set its own effort with the effort tool; code it writes itself starts at medium and up by its depth. Also settable with /gearbox effort.

navigator.title: Browser navigator
navigator.description: Model of the subagent that clicks through browser checks and only collects evidence; the main model then analyzes it. Sonnet is the default (as fast as Haiku in a side-by-side test, and steadier); Haiku is cheaper.

log.title: Debug log
log.description: Write what gearbox decides, and what each request sent, to ~/.claude/gearbox/logs/<session>.jsonl: off, on, or full (also the first 200 characters of each prompt). Also settable with /gearbox log or in /gearbox settings; it applies at once.

orchestrator.title: Orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The main conversation only plans, briefs and reviews; the work runs in lanes, one long-lived subagent per model, each started at the top effort and lowered per job. On by default, in every session, Haiku ones included; /gearbox orchestrator auto leaves a session started on Haiku shifting models instead, and off turns it off. Also settable with /gearbox orchestrator.

orchestrator_model.title: Orchestrator model
orchestrator_model.description: Model of the main conversation while the orchestrator is on. Also settable with /gearbox orchestrator-model.

orchestrator_effort.title: Orchestrator effort
orchestrator_effort.description: Effort of the main conversation while the orchestrator is on. auto (the default) sets it per prompt, xhigh at most: what the orchestrator keeps runs at the effort the rules give that work, a hand-off at high (briefing and reviewing the agent is where it is won or lost; low when the lane only relays a command), an agent's report coming back at high. The other levels pin it. Also settable with /gearbox orchestrator-effort.

orchestrator_agents.title: Orchestrator parallel agents
orchestrator_agents.description: While the orchestrator is on, the most agents a request of independent parts goes out to at once, from 1 to 6; 1 turns the fan-out off. The orchestrator decides from the survey whether a request splits and into how many, never more than this. Also settable with /gearbox orchestrator-agents.
